core_obligations: Record that the property is local in the Zariski topology (proof lines 5077-5078).

For a flat finitely presented morphism of affines with finitely many irreducible components downstairs, use that generic points lift along flat morphisms to reduce to bounding the generic points of each fibre, and bound them because the fibres are affine of finite type over a field, hence Noetherian (proof lines 5079-5090).

For a surjective flat finitely presented morphism of affines with finitely many irreducible components upstairs, descend the finiteness of the number of irreducible components along the surjective continuous map (proof lines 5091-5094).
Conclude that the three hypotheses of the locality criterion hold and obtain fppf locality (proof lines 5095-5096).
proof_roadmap: Finiteness of the number of components goes up along a flat finitely presented morphism of affines, by lifting generic points and bounding the fibres (proof lines 5079-5090).
It goes down along a surjective such morphism, by the topological statement (proof lines 5091-5094).
difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that the property of a scheme that every quasi-compact open has finitely many irreducible components is local in the fppf topology (statement lines 5069-5073). The proof works through a locality criterion, and the substance is two verifications of how the property behaves under a flat finitely presented morphism of affines. For the property of having finitely many irreducible components, generic points of the source map to generic points of the target, so it suffices to bound the generic points of each fibre, and each fibre is an affine scheme of finite type over the residue field, hence Noetherian and in particular with finitely many irreducible components (proof lines 5079-5090). For the target, the corresponding statement under a surjective flat finitely presented morphism is reduced to the topological fact that a surjective continuous map lifts a finite set of irreducible components (proof lines 5091-5094). Together with Zariski locality these are exactly the hypotheses of the criterion, so the conclusion follows (proof lines 5077-5078 and 5095-5096). The claim is H2: two distinct geometric inputs, generic points under flat maps and Noetherianness of the fibres, are used in addition to one topological input, and all three are stated with their source rather than being hidden in a single citation.
